title: tenant-prefill-delegator-telemetry-driven-quant-suggester
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Tenants with mixed traffic profiles (short chat turns mixed with occasional long-form generations) need per-tenant prefill and quantization recommendations that balance unit economics with quality. This PR introduces a telemetry-driven Prefill Delegator and a Loss-Aware Quant Suggestion engine that uses per-tenant SLO signals, token distribution histograms, and recent eval deltas to pick safe default mini-prefill sizes and quant tiers.

What this changes (summary): adds a lightweight delegator service, ties into tenant metrics ingestion, surfaces recommendations via the Optimize API, adds a CLI flag for gradual rollout, and includes guarded fallbacks for quality regressions.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-4982) [x] unit tests for decision logic [x] integration smoke tests against local runtime [x] telemetry dashboards and alerts created [x] runtime feature flag + rollout plan

Design notes: The Prefill Delegator runs as a small stateless process in the econ service (services/econ/prefill_delegator.py). It consumes tenant signals (mean latency, 95p token length, recent hallucination/regression score) from the existing telemetry stream and produces a recommended profile: {prefill_millis, prefill_tokens, quant_tier_hint}. Recommendations are persisted as tenant annotations in the tenant-config store and emitted to the Optimize API for visibility and manual acceptance. The Loss-Aware Quant Suggestion component uses a sliding-window of eval score deltas; when predicted quality impact exceeds a conservative threshold we either: 1) pin a safer quant tier, or 2) return a canary instruction (apply quant tier to 1% of traffic for 24h). Safety fallbacks: automatic rollback when the eval delta crosses threshold or customer opt-out is set.

Rollout plan: start off behind feature flag per-tenant (--prefill-delegator=opt-in), enable shadow mode (write-only recommendations) for two weeks, then enable rollout at 5% traffic with auto-rollback. We created three Canary tenants for staging evaluation and included a canary smoke test in CI.

Backwards compatibility: no runtime breaking changes. Delegator integrates via the econ service public API; defaults are conservative and will not change existing tenant profiles unless accepted by the tenant or an automated safe rollout completes.

Observability and metrics: new telemetry keys: econ.prefill.recommendation.count, econ.prefill.applied.count, econ.quant.suggested.tier, econ.quant.rollback.count. Dashboards: Tenant Prefill Recommendations (per-tenant histogram), Quant Suggestion Safety (eval deltas, rollback rate). Alerts: >2% rollback rate across tenants in 24h triggers sev3.

Performance: microbenchmarking shows the delegator decision path adds <3ms median overhead to the recommendation pipeline and the persisted annotation write adds negligible latency to tenant-config updates. See benchmarks/README for full numbers.

Security and privacy: the delegator uses already-ingested, aggregated telemetry only; no new PII is collected. Tenant annotations are access-controlled by existing RBAC rules.

Related: ENG-4982 (design), ENG-5019 (telemetry changes), SUP-3421 (customer-reported regressions used for test cases).
